async function fetch(url) {
  const { packId, path } = manifest.lookup(url)

  })

  return new Response(await pack.text(path))
}

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 1088 ms, comparable baseline 4462 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 4702 ms or baseline 58800 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 3052 ms + 1480 ms + 170 ms = 4702 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 4281 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 8983 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 4702 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 4702 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 58800 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 70897 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 485 ms, comparable baseline 4179 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 484 ms or baseline 52677 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 0 ms + 483 ms + 1 ms = 484 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 1 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 485 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 484 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 484 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 52677 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 65143 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

const packCache = new Map()

async function fetch(url) {
  const { packId, path } = manifest.lookup(url)
  const pack = await memo(packCache, packId, async () => {
    const response = await nativeFetch(packUrl(packId))
    return decodeStream(response.body)
  })

  return new Response(await pack.text(path))
}

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 1461 ms, comparable baseline 4462 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 5790 ms or baseline 58800 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 4897 ms + 859 ms + 34 ms = 5790 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 3025 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 8815 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 5790 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 5790 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 58800 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 70897 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 448 ms, comparable baseline 4179 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 447 ms or baseline 52677 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 0 ms + 447 ms + 1 ms = 447 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 0 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 448 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 447 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 447 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 52677 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 65143 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

const packCache = new Map()

async function fetch(url) {
  const { packId, path } = manifest.lookup(url)
  const pack = await memo(packCache, packId, async () => {
    const response = await nativeFetch(packUrl(packId))
    return decodeStream(response.body)
  })

  return new Response(await pack.text(path))
}

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 1280 ms, comparable baseline 4462 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 5007 ms or baseline 58800 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 4103 ms + 875 ms + 30 ms = 5007 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 5001 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 10008 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 5007 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 5007 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 58800 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 70897 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 448 ms, comparable baseline 4179 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 446 ms or baseline 52677 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 0 ms + 446 ms + 0 ms = 446 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 1 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 448 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 446 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 446 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 52677 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 65143 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

const packCache = new Map()
const fileCache = new Map()

async function fetch(url) {
  const { packId, path } = manifest.lookup(url)
  const remote = await memo(packCache, packId, () => fetchPackManifest(packUrl(packId)))

  return new Response(await memo(fileCache, url, async () => {
    const bytes = await fetchPackFile(remote, path) // buffered Range
    return text(decompress(bytes))
  }))
}

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 1109 ms, comparable baseline 4462 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 3075 ms or baseline 58800 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 3073 ms + 0 ms + 3 ms = 3075 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 7503 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 10578 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 3075 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 3075 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 58800 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 70897 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 2 ms, comparable baseline 4179 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 0 ms or baseline 52677 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 0 ms + 0 ms + 0 ms = 0 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 1 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 2 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 0 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 0 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 52677 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 65143 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

Selected strategy pseudocode 
const packCache = new Map()
const fileCache = new Map()

async function fetch(url) {
  const { packId, path } = manifest.lookup(url)
  const remote = await memo(packCache, packId, () => fetchPackManifest(packUrl(packId)))

  return new Response(await memo(fileCache, url, async () => {
    const file = await fetchPackFileStream(remote, path) // streaming Range
    return text(await readStream(file.stream))
  }))
}

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 1121 ms, comparable baseline 4462 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 3111 ms or baseline 58800 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 3107 ms + 0 ms + 4 ms = 3111 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 6539 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 9650 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 3111 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 3111 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 58800 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 70897 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 2 ms, comparable baseline 4179 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 1 ms or baseline 52677 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 0 ms + 0 ms + 0 ms = 1 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 1 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 2 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 1 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 1 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 52677 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 65143 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

const packCache = new Map()
const fileCache = new Map()

async function fetch(url) {
  const { packId, path } = manifest.lookup(url)
  const remote = await memo(packCache, packId, () => fetchPackManifest(packUrl(packId)))

  if (!started(packId)) {
    const allFiles = fetchPackFilesCompressed(remote, remote.allPaths()) // buffered Ranges
    createLazyFilePromises(fileCache, allFiles)
    materializeRemainingFilesInRaf(fileCache)
  }

  return new Response(await fileCache.get(path)) // resolves when this file is ready
}

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 878 ms, comparable baseline 4462 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 4267 ms or baseline 58800 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 2993 ms + 0 ms + 1275 ms = 4267 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 2697 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 6964 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 4267 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 4267 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 58800 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 70897 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 2 ms, comparable baseline 4179 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 0 ms or baseline 52677 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 0 ms + 0 ms + 0 ms = 0 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 1 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 2 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 0 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 0 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 52677 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 65143 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

Selected strategy pseudocode 
const packCache = new Map()
const fileCache = new Map()

async function fetch(url) {
  const { packId, path } = manifest.lookup(url)
  const remote = await memo(packCache, packId, () => fetchPackManifest(packUrl(packId)))

  if (!started(packId)) {
    const streams = fetchPackFilesStream(remote, remote.allPaths()) // streaming Ranges
    createFilePromises(fileCache, streams)
  }

  return new Response(await fileCache.get(path)) // each file resolves from its stream
}

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 1140 ms, comparable baseline 4462 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 4121 ms or baseline 58800 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 3895 ms + 0 ms + 226 ms = 4121 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 3979 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 8099 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 4121 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 4121 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 58800 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 70897 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 1 ms, comparable baseline 4179 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 0 ms or baseline 52677 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 0 ms + 0 ms + 0 ms = 0 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 1 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 1 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 0 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 0 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 52677 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

}

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 1232 ms, comparable baseline 4462 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 3313 ms or baseline 58800 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 3121 ms + 0 ms + 193 ms = 3313 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 4697 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 8011 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 3313 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 3313 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 58800 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 70897 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.

Reading the totals

Start with Comparable request window. This is the closest asset-level wall-clock comparison because it collapses overlapping request waits into a union: TP 3 ms, comparable baseline 4179 ms.

Do not read diagnostic sums as page duration. Values like TP 1 ms or baseline 52677 ms are sums across many overlapping rows. They are useful for finding where work accumulated, but they are not directly comparable to the top-level load time.

TP work breakdown = sum of unique pack/file fetch work + per-asset extract + per-asset overhead across served-from-pack assets = 0 ms + 0 ms + 1 ms = 1 ms
Excluded duplicated waits: 2 ms. Raw paused sum before excluding waits: 3 ms.

TP effective asset sum = TP work breakdown + sum of baseline-fetch ms for assets TP fell through on
= 1 ms + 0 ms (0 fall-throughs paid network cost) = 1 ms

Comparable baseline diagnostic sum = baseline fetch sum for rows TP served = 52677 ms
All observed BL asset wait sum = 65143 ms

Reading this table

  • Pack/file fetch+decode — full/stream variants show the time this request waited for pack initialization. Range-stream variants show metadata wait plus file-region fetch wait. miss is the first initializer for a pack, pending means this asset arrived while another request was already initializing the same pack, and hit means metadata/decode was already available at request start.
  • Baseline asset fetch — time to fetch this single asset over the wire in baseline mode. Adjacent for direct comparison.
  • Extract — pack.extract(file), in-memory, sub-millisecond.
  • SW overhead — total − fetch − extract. Browser-side Service Worker response construction and marker-message overhead. No Playwright/CDP fulfill path is included.
  • TokenPack total — fetch + extract + overhead. The wall-clock time spent producing this asset response.
  • Green/red coloring compares real work (fetch + extract) vs baseline fetch — i.e., what TokenPack would cost without the harness tax. Green on the TokenPack side = real work was faster than the baseline fetch.
  • outside TP manifest — baseline fetched this URL, but it is outside the comparable manifest-handled URL set for this sampled phase. This is not a TokenPack miss.
  • TP did not request — baseline fetched this comparable manifest URL, but the TokenPack run did not request it in the sampled phase. A large cluster usually means the TP page diverged or failed before reaching that import path; an isolated row can also come from feature flags, lazy imports, version drift, or conditional app flow.
  • TP-only (not in BL) — TokenPack requested this URL but baseline never did. Different code path got executed (feature flag, A/B variant, error-recovery branch).

Column sums overstate wall-clock because requests run in parallel. Iteration durations are the real answer.
